business_problem: TAG had to launch a credit-card receivables registry under strict Central Bank deadlines and security SLAs, process huge volumes of lender and merchant data, and prevent SMEs from pledging the same receivables multiple times while still keeping the platform economical and highly available.
solution_summary: TAG built its receivables-registration platform on MongoDB Atlas running on Google Cloud Platform to store and process transactional payment data for Brazil's new lending model. Atlas gives the team a cloud-native database backbone that can be provisioned through infrastructure as code, queried through one unified API, and scaled to absorb the heavy write throughput required to register pending credit-card receivables from multiple sources. Atlas Performance Advisor helps the team spot slow queries and tune indexes, Atlas Online Archive moves older data into managed object storage so the hot transactional environment stays lean, and Atlas Triggers lets TAG adjust resource usage dynamically around peak periods. The design also depends on ACID transactions and sharding so data integrity is preserved even when operations are interrupted. That combination lets TAG deliver real-time visibility to lenders while meeting Central Bank security expectations and keeping costs aligned to demand.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Serves as TAG's transactional registry for payment receivables and provides the scalable cloud database foundation for the platform.

solution_components.name: Atlas Online Archive
solution_components.role: Archives older registry data into managed object storage while keeping it queryable alongside hot data.

solution_components.name: Atlas Triggers
solution_components.role: Executes serverless resource-management logic so TAG can align Atlas consumption with traffic patterns.

solution_components.name: Atlas Performance Advisor
solution_components.role: Monitors slow queries and recommends indexes that improve performance as receivables volumes grow.

data_flow: Receivables and payment data from merchants and financial institutions is written into MongoDB Atlas, ACID transactions preserve consistency for critical updates, Atlas Triggers adjusts resources around load peaks, colder records are tiered into Atlas Online Archive, and lenders receive reports from the live registry to assess SME borrowing capacity.
business_outcome: TAG launched on time, processed 20% of Brazil's credit-card receivables on day one, now handles millions of requests per day, and gives SMEs faster access to affordable loans while protecting lenders from duplicated collateral risk.
